messages:
Maya: Quick sync — we need a small decision on SDK retry ownership + pagination window semantics across py/ts/go. TL;DR: who owns retries (transport vs consumer), and how do we expose a "page window" that keeps client memory bounded without forcing heavy shims?

Dmitri: big vote for transport-owned retries for unary calls. lets surface per-call opts but keep sane defaults. fewer footguns. :+1:

Alina: Agree for unary, but for paged streaming/iterators I think the SDK should expose retry hooks not automatic retries. e.g., consumer may want to resume at a bookmark, not silently retry and duplicate side effects.

Juan: For py/ts/go differences:
- Python: users expect generator-based paging (yield pages) and exceptions on unrecoverable errors.
- TS: async iterators are the idiomatic surface.
- Go: explicit Pager object with Next(ctx) returning (page, err).
We should keep a common mental model ("page window") but allow language idioms.

Maya: proposal: transport handles network/backoff for idempotent calls and short-lived unary retries. For paged iterators: transport offers resume semantics + an opt-in autoretry strategy. Default: no automatic page-level retry beyond transient network reconnect (idempotent token).

Dmitri: Can we codify "page window" as: SDK buffers N outstanding pages in memory (configurable), consumer gets an iterator over items, SDK fetches ahead up to window. If a fetch fails mid-window, SDK exposes a RetryError with resume_token so consumer can decide.

Alina: I like that. API sketch: (TS)
```ts
for await (const item of client.listRecords({ pageSize: 200, prefetch: 2 })) {
  // consumer code
}
```
If a prefetch fails, iterator throws RetryError containing resumeToken.

Juan: Go sketch:
```go
p := client.ListRecords(ctx, &ListOpts{PageSize:200, Prefetch:2})
for {
  page, err := p.Next()
  if err == iterator.ErrRetry { log.Println(err.ResumeToken()); /* decide */ }
  if err == io.EOF { break }
}
```

Maya: Default retry policy (transport): 3 attempts, exponential backoff with full jitter, but only for idempotent endpoints (GET-like). We need metadata from server to mark idempotency? Or we add an explicit client flag per RPC. Thoughts?

Dmitri: Server-side metadata is ideal but not reliable. Add an opt-in/annotation on client call surfaces: e.g., `callOptions.idempotent = true` at per-method generation time. For generated SDKs, mark list/get methods as idempotent by default.

Alina: Also surface a `retryStrategy` option object that can be passed to client factory for advanced users. Keep the simple defaults for 95% case.

Juan: One more: streaming vs paged: streaming (server push) should keep transport-level reconnect and resume token if offered by server. For long-lived streams we should NEVER auto-retry application-level operations that are not idempotent.

deploy-bot: Deploy preview: feature/soft-page-window rolled to canary. 3 hosts.

Maya: Action items:
- Dmitri: add opt-in idempotent flag to codegen for list/get methods (small PR).
- Alina: draft TS/py examples showing prefetch semantics and RetryError shape.
- Juan: add Go Pager API docs + error semantics to SDK spec.
- Team: agree default prefetch window = 1 (no prefetch) for memory-constrained clients, expose `prefetch` config.

Dmitri: I'll do the codegen PR today.

Alina: I'll prototype the RetryError shape: { name: 'RetryError', message, resumeToken?, retriedAttempts }. Will show examples where consumer catches and replays.

Juan: I'll doc the Go error wrapping pattern and ensure ResumeToken string is accessible.

Maya: Thanks — aim to land the changes and follow up with a short RFC update with API snippets. If anyone strongly disagrees speak up now.

Dmitri: No objections from me.

Alina: SGTM.

Juan: SGTM.

Maya: OK closing this thread. Will post RFC delta in #eng-platform later today. :rocket:
